# OMP Session Gateway

> Native integration with stock Oh My Pi (OMP) >=18.1.20. No OMP fork, custom build,
> gateway-specific OMP plugin, or publisher credential. v0.6.3 is qualified for stable promotion; publication is pending.
> Keep using OMP in the terminal; the separate gateway discovers collaboration-enabled
> sessions and opens OMP's own encrypted View/Control client in any modern browser, installable as a PWA where the platform supports it. One-time
> setup requires collab.autoStart, Bun 1.4.0, gateway installation, and TUN-mode Tailscale Serve
> with Funnel disabled. No per-session QR scan or link copy. Community project; not affiliated
> with or endorsed by the Oh My Pi maintainers.

## Supported platforms

- Supported and tested in CI on every change (the stock-OMP canaries run daily): Linux, macOS, and Windows gateway hosts; Chrome and Chromium, Edge through Chromium, Firefox, Safari/WebKit, and Android; iPhone and iPad as a WebKit browser, emulated in CI. Supported is not qualified: qualification is the exact hardware matrix below. Lanes: portable-source (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows), browser-core (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, iPhone-class WebKit), browser-notifications (Pixel sizes), windows-service-lifecycle, canary and canary-windows.

## Current qualification boundary

- v0.6.3 is qualified for stable promotion from signed candidate v0.6.3-prealpha.2 (source 9deb122584a92c3e0519f9884ae56a2c33f6a4c2, archive SHA-256 5a1ba40e79a0c3ca911d8efed0697c41a8732173573c9b2bb814961c892d6c51); a clean stable-channel build matched its 46 non-metadata runtime files. Publication is pending, and published v0.6.2 remains GitHub Latest until it succeeds. Every qualification lane passed on 2026-09-27 on its first attempt against stock OMP v18.3.0. On Windows, v0.6.3 installs and runs from a standard (non-elevated) account, which v0.6.2 could not (#293, #294), and reads its task's state in a way that also works for a standard user over SSH. No claim for arbitrary builds from main.
- Exact OMP v18.3.0 source: 62bc57be1b03ef0802a33cf7f5f530e534527531. Set only collab.autoStart (off/view/control); start participating sessions with plain omp. The gateway reads OMP discovery and queries each host; OMP does not register with the gateway.
- Debian 13 (trixie) x86-64, Linux 6.12.94+deb13-amd64: 83/83 migration/recovery invariants, stock OMP publication/revocation, persistence, tagged-identity denial/exposure, uninstall and resource teardown.
- Mac14,3 / macOS 26.6.1 arm64: doctor 18/18, rollback 23/23, install/rotation/reboot-to-login persistence, real allowlisted identity and forged-header/exposure checks. Positive allowed-user HTTPS was measured on Mac/Pixel, not the tagged Debian CI caller.
- Windows Server 2025 x86-64, build 26100, on a disposable VM destroyed afterwards: as Administrator, the candidate upgraded published v0.6.2, survived a real reboot and started automatically 99.2 s after interactive logon; doctor 15/18 with only the tagged node's identity, PWA and session checks false; named-pipe publication, View/Control 200, stale generations 409, the Pixel's View and Control, readiness rotation, history-selected rollback and uninstall. Then a standard local account, its token without Administrators or SeSecurityPrivilege, installed the candidate fresh, and after a real reboot the gateway started 46.0 s after that account's logon; doctor 15/18, readiness rotation and uninstall passed as that account. The claim is start at interactive logon, not at boot.
- Pixel 10 Pro / Android 17 build CP3A.260905.009 / Chrome 153.0.8010.53: View read-only, Control writable, prompt accepted, return to directory; same-page recovery measured at a 250 ms probe cadence: unlock 7,520 ms (including device wake), Airplane 5,671 ms, Doze 383 ms; all seven forbidden capability sinks detectable and clean.
- Background Web Push on the same Pixel with the installed app closed: Private, Session and Preview delivery on the lock screen in 3.1–4.2 s, one notification each; taps to current Control and View, stale-generation scrub, authoritative clear, permission revocation, lock/resume, Wi-Fi and cellular delivery, Airplane suppression and recovery; ten forbidden sinks clean. Force-stop and Doze outcomes are observed variants, never delivery guarantees.
- Real cloud devices on TestingBot (ADR-032), qualified in the browser: iPhone 17 Pro Max / iOS 26.6 / Safari 26.6, iPad (9th generation) / iPadOS 26.6 / Safari 26.6, and Galaxy S26 (SM-S942B) / Android 16 / Chrome 145.0.7632.159 each passed View read-only, Control writable, prompt accepted and return to directory on the candidate's app bundle, with seven detectable clean capability sinks; TestingBot's test records held no live link, video or screenshots. On the iPhone, the Home Screen app enabled alerts with a real tap, an attention alert arrived in 10.3 s with the app in the background, and its tap opened current Control with a scrubbed address. Limits: Serve saw the workstation's allowlisted login, not a phone's; alerts were proven unlocked with the app in the background, not on the lock screen; lock, Airplane, Doze, force-stop and cellular behavior stay Pixel-only.
- Tailscale Serve over tailnet HTTPS only, TUN mode required, Funnel disabled. Fresh relay check: 1,800 seconds (2026-09-27T05:43:28.698Z–06:13:28.705Z), two transitions, final phase live. The 30-minute check replaces eight hours, as for every mainline release; eight-hour endurance was not rerun or claimed, no historical endurance transfers, and residual prolonged-operation risk is accepted. No bounded-memory-growth claim is made.
- Other Windows versions are supported and CI-tested, including a daily canary that drives stock OMP's named pipe through the gateway, but not qualified. Specialized attention and branch/resume, and new media qualification remain unqualified/unadvertised. Seeded-fixture product media is not release-qualification evidence for these lanes. Android radio changes can still wedge Chrome; the proven same-page recoveries do not remove that limit.
- v0.6.2 is the migration/rollback predecessor. It cannot be installed or run from a standard Windows account (#293, #294), so rolling back to it on Windows needs an elevated install. Gateway rollback does not switch OMP. v0.6.0, further back, cannot enable background alerts on iPhone or iPad, because it rejects WebKit's push subscription, which leaves out a null expiration time.
- In v0.5.0 and earlier, the first visit after a gateway upgrade can navigate a pending launch or an open View/Control page back to the directory: the service worker cannot see that a page is in use because Chromium reports each page's creation URL. The first post-release View/Control smoke failures match this navigation. The v0.5.1 fix never navigates from the worker.
- The v0.6.3 published-byte local/Pixel smoke is pending after publication. The v0.6.2 smoke passed on its first attempt across the upgrade from v0.6.1, against Bun's global stock OMP 18.1.20.

## Fork-era release history

- v0.3.0 requires its exact patched OMP v18.1.14 and matching historical instructions. Its qualification does not transfer to the mainline architecture.
